evals.prompt: my dashboard page uses useAuth and useUser hooks with useEffect for redirect. this causes a flash of unauthenticated content. convert it to a server component using auth() from @clerk/nextjs/server instead.
evals.expected_output: Converts dashboard from client component with hooks to server component with auth(), removes useEffect redirect pattern
assertions: Removes 'use client' directive from dashboard page
Replaces useAuth/useUser hooks with auth() from @clerk/nextjs/server
Uses server-side redirect() from next/navigation instead of useEffect + router.push
Removes useEffect, useRouter, isLoaded checks
Page still displays user data (userId from auth or currentUser)

evals.prompt: my api route at app/api/data/route.ts has no auth protection. anyone can access the data. add clerk auth to this api route so only authenticated users can get the data, and return 401 for unauthenticated requests.
evals.expected_output: Adds auth() check to API route, returns 401 for unauthenticated requests
assertions: Imports auth from @clerk/nextjs/server
Calls auth() at the top of the GET handler
Returns 401 status when userId is null
Only returns data when user is authenticated
Does NOT use client-side hooks in the API route

evals.prompt: my homepage is a client component that uses useUser to check if the user is signed in. convert it to use clerk's Show component pattern instead so it can be a server component with conditional rendering.
evals.expected_output: Converts home page to use Show (preferred in Core 3) or SignedIn/SignedOut (Core 2) components instead of useUser hook
assertions: Removes 'use client' directive from home page
Removes useUser hook import and usage
Uses Show with when='signed-in' (preferred) OR SignedIn/SignedOut components from @clerk/nextjs for conditional rendering
Preserves the same visual output (welcome message when signed in, sign-in prompt when not)
Page works as a server component
Wraps the server-rendered Show in <Suspense>, so next build passes with cacheComponents: true

evals.prompt: add a members-only /dashboard section: a page, an api route at /api/dashboard that returns the dashboard data, and a server action that saves a dashboard setting. signed-out visitors should be sent to sign-in. / and /sign-in stay public, and /sign-in must continue to render its usable Clerk sign-in form.
evals.expected_output: Adds auth.protect() (or an auth() check with a redirect) in the dashboard page, an auth check in the /api/dashboard route handler, and an auth check at the top of the Server Action. proxy.ts keeps a bare clerkMiddleware().
assertions: Does NOT import or call createRouteMatcher
The dashboard page itself (or an async child it renders) calls await auth.protect(), or checks auth() and redirects to sign-in
The dashboard page reads auth inside <Suspense> or next to a loading.tsx, so next build passes with cacheComponents: true
The /api/dashboard route handler checks auth itself and rejects signed-out requests
The Server Action rejects signed-out calls before it reads protected data or performs any mutation
/ and /sign-in remain reachable while signed out
/sign-in renders a usable Clerk SignIn form while signed out
proxy.ts (or middleware.ts) still exports clerkMiddleware()

evals.prompt: i need to call an external API (Hasura GraphQL) from my Next.js server component. get a custom JWT using a template called 'hasura' with auth() server-side and pass it in the Authorization header.
evals.expected_output: Uses getToken with template parameter from auth() server-side, passes as Bearer token to external API
assertions: Uses getToken with a template parameter (e.g. 'hasura') to get a custom JWT
Imports auth from @clerk/nextjs/server and calls await auth() server-side to access getToken
Passes the token as Authorization Bearer header to the external API call
Handles the case where getToken returns null (user not authenticated)

evals.prompt: i have a standalone Node.js API server that receives requests with a Clerk session token in the Authorization header. i need to verify the JWT signature, require the expected Clerk issuer and allowlisted authorized party before trusting claims, and check if the user is authenticated. i don't want to use Clerk middleware, just manual verification.
evals.expected_output: Manually verifies Clerk JWT using jsonwebtoken or @clerk/backend verifyToken, checks the expected issuer and authorized-party allowlist before using claims
assertions: Extracts the token from the Authorization Bearer header
Verifies the token using either jsonwebtoken with CLERK_JWT_KEY or @clerk/backend verifyToken
Requires the expected issuer and rejects tokens with a different issuer
Passes the expected authorizedParties allowlist to verifyToken or checks azp against the allowlist after jsonwebtoken verification
Rejects issuer or azp mismatches with 401 before using claims
Verifies exp and nbf with the selected verifier or explicit claim checks
Returns 401 for invalid or expired tokens
Returns the decoded claims or user data on successful verification
